reasoning: The Fed cut three times in late 2025 to 3.50-3.75% and then held in early 2026. Kevin Warsh is expected to take over as chair around mid-2026 and is likely to favor cuts. Against that, the energy-price and inflation shock from the 2026 Middle East conflict appeared to push market pricing toward fewer cuts in 2026. A divided committee and sticky inflation make holds the default at any given meeting. A September cut remains plausible under a new dovish-leaning chair, especially if the labor market softens, and a hike is unlikely but not impossible. I put the probability of no change at slightly above even.
